transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Occupational health sent me. They, uh... they think I'm not eating enough. I don't really see the problem, but... I guess most days it's just black coffee. Maybe a plain yogurt later, or a few bites of chicken at night. Eating a full meal just... it feels like I'm letting my standards slip.
What do you mean by 'letting your standards slip' when you think about eating a full meal?

It's... just about discipline. People at work say one thing about how I look, but... I don't see what they see. When I look in the mirror, I'm mostly just... looking at my stomach. My waist. If I eat a full meal, I lose that. I guess I just... I judge my whole day by whether I look lean enough to actually respect myself.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as being overweight?
I don't... I don't know if I'd use that word. I'm not really sure. I just... I just see that it's not where it needs to be.
Have you lost a lot of weight recently?

I guess so. My uniform... it hangs off me now. I've had to tighten my duty belt past the old notches just to keep it up. The nurse out front said my weight was dangerously low, but... I don't know. I heard that and just thought... I could still stand to be a little sharper.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I... yeah. I suppose I am. If I step on the scale and it's up... even just half a pound, I get this... this jolt. Like things are slipping out of my control. I end up spending the rest of the shift cutting back even harder, because... I just can't stand the thought of putting it back on.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you can't stop?
No. I don't do that. I keep things... pretty tight.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No. I don't... I don't do that.
Do you exercise a lot?
No. Not really. Just... whatever I have to do for work. I don't spend hours at the gym or anything like that.
Do you think your weight is connected to your self-worth?

I don't know if I'd use the word self-worth. But... I guess. It's just... when I look in the mirror, I don't see what everyone else claims they see. I just focus on my stomach. My waist. And... if I don't look lean enough, I just can't respect myself. It pretty much decides how my whole day is going to go.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict what you eat?

I suppose so. It's... yeah. If the scale is up, even just half a pound, I get this jolt. Like I've completely lost control. So I'll just spend the rest of the day cutting back harder... I just can't stand the idea of putting weight back on.
When you say you don't see what others see when you look in the mirror, what is it that you think they see?

I don't really know. You'd have to ask them. They just... they say I look fine, I guess. Or they tell me I don't need to lose anything else. I don't really get it. I just know what's actually there when I look.
When you look in the mirror, do you think your body shape or weight is different from what it actually is?

I... look, I think I already said this. I don't think I'm seeing things that aren't there, if that's what you're getting at. I just focus on my stomach. My waist. If it's not lean enough, I can't respect myself, and that dictates my day. I don't know why other people claim they see something else... I'm just looking at the facts.
Do you think your stomach or waist is actually larger than it appears to other people?
I... I don't know. Like I said, you'd have to ask them. I just see what I see.
Do you think your waist is larger than it actually is?
No. I... I'm not imagining things. It's exactly the size that it is. I just see it for what it is.
Do you think you would be able to accept yourself if you gained a small amount of weight?

No. I... I don't think so. If the scale goes up... even just half a pound, I get this... jolt. Like I've completely lost control. I'd just spend the rest of the day cutting back harder. I just... I can't stand the idea of putting weight back on. I wouldn't accept it.
Do you think you are underweight?

I mean... my uniform hangs off me now. I've had to punch new holes in my belt just to keep it up. But... when the nurse took my weight earlier and said it was dangerously low, I just... I didn't see it that way. I still thought I could stand to be a little sharper. So, no. I don't think I am.
Do you think you would still feel the need to restrict your food intake if you couldn't see yourself in the mirror or measure your weight?
I... I don't really know. I've never thought about it. I always have access to a scale, so... I couldn't tell you what I'd do if I didn't. I just don't know.
Is your goal of being lean more about achieving a certain appearance or more about not gaining weight?

I suppose... it's about what I see. When I look in the mirror, I just... I don't see what the doctors or my wife claim is there. I look at my stomach, my waist... and if it's not lean enough, I just... I can't respect myself. The whole day is ruined. So, it's the appearance, I guess.
Is your main goal in restricting your food intake to avoid gaining weight or to maintain a specific body shape?

I suppose it's both. Like I said, it's what I see in the mirror, but... the number matters too. 

If the scale is up even half a pound, I... I get this jolt. Like I've completely lost control. I'll usually just spend the rest of the day cutting back harder. I just... I can't stand the idea of putting weight back on.
